cases.subject: Posiedzenie rady - pytanie o politykę dywidendy
cases.body:
Szanowny Panie Prezesie,

przygotowując porządek posiedzenia rady nadzorczej na 3.02.2027, zauważyłem, że w projekcie budżetu nie ma jednoznacznego zapisu o polityce dywidendy za 2026 rok. Rada zapyta o to na pewno, bo akcjonariusze oczekują jasnego stanowiska zarządu przed zatwierdzeniem sprawozdania.

Chciałbym zapytać Pana wprost: jaką część zysku za 2026 rok zarząd zamierza wnioskować do wypłaty w formie dywidendy, a jaką zatrzymać na inwestycje w flotę? Interesuje mnie Pana osobiste stanowisko w tej sprawie, a nie opinia działu finansowego. Jeżeli zarząd nie ma jeszcze jednej propozycji, proszę o wskazanie wariantów, które rozważa Pan z pierwszeństwem.

Rada oczekuje od zarządu jasnej informacji, bo od stanowiska w sprawie dywidendy zależy także ocena ryzyka związanego z zadłużeniem spółki po zakupie floty. Dodatkowo proszę o krótkie uzasadnienie, jak ten wybór wpływa na zaplanowany kredyt na zakup naczep. Rada będzie dyskutować oba tematy łącznie, więc zależy mi na spójnej odpowiedzi.

Chodzi mi także o to, aby wersje liczbowe, które Pan przedstawi, były zgodne z tabelą w projekcie budżetu, ponieważ rozbieżności w tej sprawie rada traktuje bardzo poważnie. Odpowiedź proszę przekazać mi mailem przed posiedzeniem, najlepiej w ciągu kilku dni, żebym mógł uwzględnić ją w przygotowanych materiałach.

cases.subject: Delivery windows: our new unloading schedule from February
cases.body:
Dear Mr Szalewski,

for your information, we have changed the unloading schedule at our central warehouse in Gothenburg. The changes start on 02.02.2027 and apply to all inbound shipments from Poland.

The new unloading windows are Monday to Friday from 07:00 to 11:00 and from 13:00 to 16:00. On Saturdays, we receive only pre-booked pallets for chilled products. Trucks that arrive outside the booked window wait until the next free gate, so the earlier booking process, which your dispatchers know from the previous months, continues to apply.

The gate capacity has also been increased. We now have six gates in the morning shift instead of four, and this should reduce the average waiting time for trucks from about 90 minutes to under 40. Our logistics team reports that the first results of the test period in January were positive, with 94 percent of trucks unloaded within the booked window.

Please note that the loading ramp number 5 is closed for maintenance until the end of February. Trucks with chilled goods are directed to ramps 1 to 3, which are closer to the cold store. Our team will mark the new route on the gate signs.

We share this information so that your planning team has the current picture. No action is needed on your side.

Best regards | Karin Lindqvist | Procurement Lead | Nordic Foods Trade

cases.subject: Re: Partners' meeting 5.02 in Gdansk - confirmed
cases.body:
Dear Mr Szalewski,

thank you for confirming that you will join the partners' meeting in Gdansk in person on 5 February. The room is booked, and I am writing to share the current plan so that you have the full picture.

The meeting starts at 10:00 and ends at 15:30. The agenda has four parts: the review of the joint tenders from the last quarter, the results of the prequalification for the Baltic tender, the new split of the work between our two companies, and the plan for the next twelve months. A working lunch is planned for 13:00.

Our team will bring a one-page summary of the open tenders, with the expected values and the dates of the decisions. We expect three of our partners from Riga and Tallinn, and two people from the Kordelan export team will join the part about customs procedures. Hotel rooms for our guests are reserved by our office, so you do not need to arrange anything.

If the schedule changes, I will let you know. There is nothing further for you to do at this stage.

Kind regards | Daniel Hargreaves | Managing Partner | Baltic Freight Partners

cases.subject: Board calendar for February and March
cases.body:
Dear Mr Szalewski,

I would like to inform you about the calendar of the supervisory board for the next two months, so that you can plan your own schedule in good time. The dates below are final and were agreed with all members on Tuesday.

The main session of the board takes place on 3 February at 10:00 in the headquarters. The audit committee meets on the same day at 08:00, before the main session. The next ordinary session is planned for 3 March, also at 10:00, and the session with the external auditor is fixed for 24 March at 14:00.

Two events outside the regular sessions are also planned. The first is the visit of the board to the Poznan warehouse in the second half of February, and the second is the investor dinner in Vienna on 5 February. I will confirm the exact details of both events separately, as soon as the organisers send their final programmes.

All members have received the invitations with the dates, and the secretary of the council keeps the calendar up to date. This message is for your information only, and I do not expect an answer.

Z powazaniem | Zbigniew Orlowicz | Przewodniczacy Rady Nadzorczej
